global_description: A dual-aesthetic motion graphic tracking the journey of a single water droplet through the complete hydrological cycle, alternating between textured pictorial illustrations and technical blueprint schematics.
prompt:
An educational motion graphic animation illustrating the continuous journey of water through nature, alternating between warm-toned hand-drawn illustrations and intricate navy blueprint schematics, matching the dynamic rhythm and visual styling demonstrated in the reference clip.

Before the reference clip, the animation establishes the droplet's initial descent and plant uptake. A falling raindrop reflecting an upside-down landscape transitions into an aerodynamic droplet blueprint, followed by a raindrop splash producing ripples in a lily pond. These ripples dissolve into a blueprint cross-section of tree xylem vessels that convey fluids upward. The fluid ascends into an illustrated tree trunk and canopy, followed by a blueprint revealing leaf vein distribution and stomatal pore regulation.

The animation then reproduces the sequence seen in the reference clip: an illustrated close-up of a leaf expelling moisture through dashed vertical arrows pulls back to reveal an expansive forest canopy. Above the trees, moisture condenses into a white cumulus cloud that rapidly builds vertically, its base darkening with falling rain. The screen transitions into a dark blue technical blueprint schematic of the cumulonimbus cloud, complete with detailed charge stratification (+ and - symbols), updraft vector arrows, rain shafts, and an electric field graph at the bottom. A sharp blueprint lightning bolt strikes downward toward a tree symbol, immediately cutting into a vivid pictorial illustration of a stormy landscape where a bright lightning strike illuminates a dark gray sky and hits a tree, with rain lashing across the field.

Following the reference clip, a single droplet falling from the storm is tracked downward, dissolving into a blueprint watershed drainage network where glowing nodes pulse along converging stream channels. The camera transitions to a topographical pictorial map tracking the river as it empties into the ocean. An ocean blueprint highlights subsurface currents and solar exposure, leading to an illustrated seascape where evaporation arrows lift from the water at dawn. A molecular blueprint shows liquid H2O breaking into vapor under solar radiation, and the camera zooms through misty clouds to isolate a newly coalesced spherical droplet, finishing on a blueprint display centered around the droplet labeled 'one drop'.

global_description: A clean, 2D illustrated motion graphic presents a step-by-step procedural recipe for making a Negroni cocktail, sequencing through glass preparation, three measured pours, stirring, and garnishing alongside coordinated UI cards and a bottom timeline.
prompt:
An instructional 2D motion graphic with clean hand-drawn line art and a warm paper-like background demonstrates a Negroni cocktail recipe, matching the layout, typography, and visual assets shown in the reference image. The video starts before the reference scene: the title 'NEGRONI' drops into the top center letter by letter in bold coral letters, followed by 'a 30 second recipe' transitioning into 'equal parts · stirred · on the rocks'. The tumbler glass outline animates into existence on the left, a bottom stepper displays six stages ('ICE', 'GIN', 'CAMPARI', 'VERMOUTH', 'STIR', 'PEEL'), and a rounded recipe card appears on the right. For Step 1, three ice cubes fall into the glass as the card tracks 'FILL ICE' with a 3-part progress bar before node 1 receives a checkmark. In Step 2, a 'GIN london dry' bottle enters, tilts, and pours clear liquid up to the '1 oz' line while the card monitors '1 OZ GIN' to '1.0 / 1 oz', after which node 2 checks off.

The animation then progresses into the state depicted in the reference image for Step 3: the card shows 'STEP 3 OF 6', '1 OZ', 'CAMPARI', 'the bitter one · 30 ml', and an active progress bar at '0.4 / 1 oz'. The red Campari bottle tilts from the upper left, pouring a red liquid stream into the glass, raising the liquid level past the ice cubes toward the '2 oz' guide line. The pour completes, the bottle withdraws, and node 3 checks off. Next, Step 4 shows a dark 'ROSSO vermouth' bottle pouring sweet vermouth up to the '3 oz' level while the card tracks '1 OZ SWEET VERMOUTH', turning the cocktail deep ruby. In Step 5, a bar spoon enters and swirls the mixture side to side while a card counts down '20 sec STIR until nice and cold' before retracting. In Step 6, an orange peel twist descends, sprays tiny yellow oil droplets, and rests over the ice as the card marks 'ORANGE PEEL express the oils, drop it in'. The sequence concludes with all six bottom nodes checked and the right card displaying 'THAT'S A NEGRONI!', 'CIN CIN!', '1:1:1', and 'gin · campari · sweet vermouth' beside the completed drink.

global_description: The animation demonstrates Fourier epicycles by showing how rotating chained circles synthesize 1D periodic waveforms and complex 2D shapes, concluding with a tribute to Joseph Fourier and digital applications.
prompt: Create an educational motion graphic animation explaining Fourier epicycles and wave synthesis, adopting the visual style, motion mechanics, and typographic hierarchy demonstrated in the reference clip. In the reference clip, set against a dark navy canvas, a chained epicycle assembly on the left sequentially adds smaller, faster-spinning circles from 2 up to 49 circles, projecting via a dashed horizontal guideline to transform an undulating wave on the right into a sharp square wave with visible Gibbs ringing, accompanied by the mathematical formula 'f(x) = 4/π (sin x + 1/3 sin 3x + 1/5 sin 5x + ...)' and sequential headers: 'Add a circle ⅓ the size, spinning 3x faster.', 'Then ⅕ the size, 5x faster...', 'Keep adding smaller, faster circles...', and '...and the wave turns square.'. Before this clip occurs, the video opens with a dynamic demonstration where a cluster of white epicycles traces a complete glowing golden treble clef under the title 'Only spinning circles drew this.'. The scene then introduces the 1D projection concept with just a single rotating circle under 'Start with one spinning circle.' and 'Track its height: a wave.', plotting a pure golden sine wave before transitioning into the sequence seen in the reference clip. Following the reference clip, add the final circle to reach 50, then modify the circle radii and harmonics to demonstrate other waveforms: it transitions into a sawtooth wave under 'Change the sizes: a sawtooth.' with the formula 'f(x) = 2/π (sin x - 1/2 sin 2x + 1/3 sin 3x - ...)', followed by a triangle wave under 'Or a triangle. Any wave at all.' with the formula 'f(x) = 8/π² (sin x - 1/9 sin 3x + 1/25 sin 5x - ...)'. The visual then transitions from 1D to 2D Fourier series under 'Now let the circles spin in 2D...' with the complex exponential formula 'z(t) = ∑ c_n e^{int}', chaining up to 301 circles that spin in the plane to trace the intricate treble clef. The video transitions to a circular portrait of Joseph Fourier with the text '1807: Joseph Fourier claims any wave is a sum of simple waves.' and 'Today his idea runs inside every MP3, JPEG and Wi-Fi signal.', then demonstrates epicycles drawing a cyan-green dual-triangle logo ('Even this logo: 301 circles.' / 'made with HyperFrames'), before concluding on the spinning epicycles drawing the golden treble clef under the title 'Only spinning circles drew this.'.

global_description: An infographic architectural animation explaining the structural mechanics, component assembly, and historical evolution of Chinese traditional Dougong brackets from the Tang to Qing dynasties using architectural line drawings, diagrams, and historical timelines.
prompt: Create an architectural motion graphics video explaining the structural mechanism and historical evolution of Chinese traditional Dougong brackets, designed with a vintage sepia-toned parchment background and technical black line illustrations. The video begins by showing a cross-sectional technical drawing of the Tang Dynasty bracket from the East Main Hall of Foguang Temple, comparing its scale side-by-side with a Qing Dynasty bracket from the Forbidden City's Wenyuange. Dimension brackets highlight their dramatic size difference: the Tang bracket accounts for 1/2 of column height, while the Qing bracket is reduced to 1/5. The animation then analyzes the cantilever mechanics of Foguang Temple's 3.7-meter eave overhang, demonstrating that the Dougong carries the outer purlin nearly 2 meters beyond what simple rafters can support. Next, an isometric step-by-step assembly animates the components: the capital block '斗', transverse arm '拱', secondary blocks, successive outward layers ('跳'), and the diagonal cantilever timber '昂'. The video then settles into the exact visual state shown in the reference image: a detailed side-section schematic of the Tang Dougong at Foguang Temple (dated 857 on the upper dynasty timeline bar). A bold red lever line traces diagonally through the Ang, labeled '挑檐' at the elevated roof eave end, pivoting over a fulcrum labeled '支点', with the interior tail pinned firmly by the roof beam labeled '梁压昂尾', accompanied by the explanatory text '昂 斜置的长木' and bottom citations from the Yingzao Fashi. Following this explanation of the lever mechanism, the video moves chronologically to display early precedents in Han stone pillars and Northern Dynasty cave temples. It narrates Liang Sicheng and Lin Huiyin's 1937 field discovery in Mount Wutai where temple beam inscriptions verified the 857 AD construction date. Next, a three-stage stylistic chart compares '豪劲', '醇和', and '羁直' periods. Sectional diagrams of Qing construction illustrate how the beam head directly took over the load, flattening the Ang into a decorative carving and turning Dougong into dense decorative trim under the eaves. Isometric diagrams then explain the modular proportion systems ('材' in Song and '斗口' in Qing). A multi-building comparative chart plots eleven historical structures along a timeline, tracking the bracket-to-column ratio dropping from 1/2 to 1/5, before concluding with a comparison between the Chinese Dougong system and the Greek Doric order.

events: Claude tool search and card reveal
global_description: A product workflow and promotional video demonstrates Verde as a unified organizational memory layer that synchronizes a refund policy update across Claude, the Verde knowledge base, ChatGPT, and Cursor.
prompt:
A dynamic product showcase demonstrates how Verde seamlessly propagates updated company knowledge into developer workflows and conversational AI.

Prior to the reference clip, the demo begins in Claude, where Maya types: 'We just agreed: annual plans get a 30-day refund window, not 14. Save it to Verde for the team.' Claude invokes Verde, marks the prior 14-day document superseded, and displays an embedded policy card. Clicking this card opens the Verde knowledge base ('getverde.ai/t/northwind') in dark mode, showing the document 'Annual plans have a 30-day refund window' with 'Published' and 'Current' tags, complete policy text, and a supersession log. Next, ChatGPT opens and receives the customer scenario question: 'A customer on an annual plan wants a refund three weeks in. Can we do that?'. ChatGPT references Verde's updated document and explains that three weeks is valid because the old 14-day limit was superseded.

During the reference clip, a dark Cursor editor window is featured with 'faq.ts' visible on the left and Cursor Composer on the right. The user prompt reads: 'Make the pricing FAQ match our refund policy.' The system processes 'Searching Verde...', identifies 'Verde 30-day refund window', and proceeds with 'Editing faq.ts...'. In the code window, the line "a: 'Yes, within 14 days of purchase.'," turns red with a minus indicator, and directly beneath it, "a: 'Yes, within 30 days of purchase or renewal.'," appears highlighted in green with a plus indicator. Composer displays a file delta tag 'faq.ts +1 -1' and writes the completion message: 'Updated the refund answer to 30 days, matching the current policy in Verde.'

After the reference clip, the editor dissolves into a dark fluted background. A glowing green Verde emblem sits at the center, flanked by Claude and ChatGPT on the left, and Cursor and 'Any MCP client' on the right. Glowing dotted data streams pulse horizontally through Verde between the tools, while the slogan 'One memory. Every AI tool.' fades in below the diagram before the video gently fades to black.
